findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables, committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or repository read access obtains these long-lived credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are visible in plaintext to any principal able to read the function configuration, with no customer-managed key policy to restrict access.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unfixed.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or NACL boundary, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the code is compromised.
The trust policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so the role assumption is not scoped to this account's functions.
